video_title: The Fastbreak: Bulls sign Norman Powell, extend Zach Collins, what's next this offseason

quotes.speaker: K.C. Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Norman Powell's two-year deal provides the Bulls with trade flexibility
quotes.excerpt: That second-year team option makes Norman Powell immediately tradeable.
quotes.quote: Let's start with the Bulls agreeing to terms with Norman Powell on a two-year, $45 million deal. By now, if you're watching this, you know the second year is a team option. This to me is a fantastic deal on so many levels. Let's start with the financial components. That second-year team option makes Norman Powell immediately tradeable. If the Bulls want to pivot off Norman Powell at next February's trade deadline, and some team wants to add a very, very good player in Norman Powell and gives the Bulls quite a haul, the Bulls have turned a free agency signing and cap space this summer into a nice trade package next February.

quotes.speaker: K.C. Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Norman Powell's offensive versatility and veteran experience will benefit the Bulls
quotes.excerpt: This is a guy who does not need a lot of touches or high usage to be impactful.
quotes.quote: This is a guy who in 11 seasons has a true shooting percentage over 60 percent. His last two seasons have been two of his best, his usage rate has been two of his highest. This is a guy who is known as a good teammate, a good leader. He's got veteran savvy, veteran knowledge that he will be imparting to young players. The future, sorry Norman Powell, haven't met you yet, is not about Norman Powell in Chicago. It's about Caleb Wilson and Dalyn Swain and Modest Musellas in Chicago. Norman Powell will immensely help all three of these players, not only with his ability to shoot and to create spacing, but also with that veteran savvy and knowledge that he has gleaned in his 11 seasons in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: K.C. Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Collins' health and versatility make him a valuable addition to the Bulls
quotes.excerpt: When healthy, Zach Collins checks a lot of boxes for Bryson Graham and Thiago Splitter.
quotes.quote: When healthy, Zach Collins checks a lot of boxes for Bryson Graham and Thiago Splitter and their vision. He is a rugged rebounder, solid rim-protecting defender, ability to run offense through him offensively, can shoot from distance to help with spacing. And look, he doesn't need to play 82 games. He is part of a big man rotation with the aforementioned Nick Claxton. Jaylen Smith can play, scale up or down depending on the lineup at either four or five. So you've got some rotating players there that can form a solid big man trio and help the Bulls in terms of their style of play.

quotes.speaker: K.C. Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Zach Collins' offensive rebounding ability to Donovan Clingan
quotes.excerpt: Zach Collins is not Donovan Clingan level offensive rebounder, but when healthy, he has been very consistent.
quotes.quote: Let's compare Zach Collins to Donovan Clingan. Why am I doing that? Well, Thiago Splitter in his introductory news conference talked about how the Portland Trail Blazers routinely shot open three-pointers and did not connect at a high clip but kept taking them. Why? Because they were elite at crashing the offensive glass and Clingan was one of the best in the league, third in the NBA in fact, at 4.5 offensive rebounds per game. Now Zach Collins is not Donovan Clingan level offensive rebounder, but when healthy, he has been a very consistent offensive rebounder throughout his career. So he will help with style of play.

quotes.speaker: K.C. Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Bulls need to address their shooting guard position using their remaining cap space
quotes.excerpt: The Bulls still have a pretty glaring need at the shooting guard.
quotes.quote: The Bulls still have a pretty glaring need at the shooting guard and basically for spacing in general. Now they've got the $9.4 million room exception left with which to sign a player. They could also acquire a player via trade into that exception. For those looking at the Anthony Simons pipe dream, I do think he's looking at a pay cut. I don't see him taking a pay cut from the mid-20s to the room exception of $9.4 million. And I can tell you with certainty that some pretty high-profile teams have kicked the tires on Anthony Simons. Those are to my knowledge the Miami Heat, the Dallas Mavericks, the Golden State Warriors. It's kind of slim pickings as far as free agent shooters still available. Gary Trent Jr. is a name that comes to mind, becomes somewhat one-dimensional at this stage of his career. Josh Okogie is kind of a well-traveled veteran, more of a defensive-minded player, but has shown some prowess from the three-point range at times.

quotes.speaker: K.C. Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Bulls Summer League roster and coaching staff preparations
quotes.excerpt: Thiago Splitter and his staff are assembling the Bulls Summer League roster.
quotes.quote: Thiago Splitter and his staff are assembling the Bulls Summer League roster for a Sunday night dinner I'm told, and I believe the first practice is scheduled for next week Monday. Obviously this is Thiago Splitter and his staff's chance to put their first impression and start putting their philosophy in place at the Advocate Center. I've been reporting pretty consistently that West Unseld Jr. will be on that staff. The rest of the staff is still being filled out as we speak. When they assemble for practice next week, it's Caleb Wilson, it's Dalyn Swain, it's obviously a lot of big names like Noah Senge, all people getting reps in, working together for the first time at the Advocate Center under Thiago Splitter in informal practices.
